title: Completion map
statement:
Let $X,\Lambda,I,P_n=\Lambda/I^n$ and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ be the coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]: $\Lambda$ is commutative Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated, $\Lambda/I$ is torsion as an additive group, and every $P_n$ is perfect over $\Lambda$. All complexes below are complexes of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with derived-category localization $Q$ and cone/shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Fix a representative $G^\bullet$ of $K$ and a K-flat resolution $F^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Write $e:Q(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ for the resulting isomorphism. Use the same $F$ at every level to form the strict tower
$$T_n=F\otimes_{\Lambda_X}(P_n)_X,\qquad t_{n+1,n}=1_F\otimes(P_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow P_n),\qquad a_n:F\to T_n,\quad x\mapsto x\otimes1.$$
Here tensor and the identifications $Q(T_n)=K_n$ are those of [def-weil-derived-tensor], with all reductions regarded as $\Lambda_X$-objects. The maps $a_n$ obey $t_{n+1,n}a_{n+1}=a_n$ strictly.

Form the termwise product complex $B=\prod_{n\geq1}T_n$ and the chain map $s:B\to B$ with $\operatorname{pr}_ns=t_{n+1,n}\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Products of these module sheaves exist and are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]; hence $Q(B)$ represents $\prod_nK_n$ by [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core]. For this definition choose the explicit complex model
$$C=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B\to B)[-1],\qquad R\varprojlim_nK_n:=Q(C).$$
This is the particular derived-limit triple of [def-weil-pbc-adic-derived-inverse-limit] furnished by this cone model, rather than an arbitrary previously chosen triangle. Explicitly, with the stated cone convention,
$$C^j=B^{j-1}\oplus B^j,\qquad d_C(y,x)=(-d_By-(1-s)x,d_Bx).$$
Let $a:F\to B$ have components $a_n$. Define the chain map $j:F\to C$ by $j^j(x)=(0,a^j(x))$, using the strict equality $(1-s)a=0$. The completion map is
$$\operatorname{comp}_K:=Q(j)\circ e^{-1}:K\longrightarrow Q(C)=R\varprojlim_nK_n.$$
The projection $C\to B$, $(y,x)\mapsto x$, followed by its $n$-th projection takes this map to the quotient arrow $K\to K_n$. In this model a strict map of reduction towers acts on $C$ by the product map in both coordinates; thus the phrase 'induced by the compatible quotient arrows' specifies the displayed chain map, not an unspecified lift into a chosen distinguished triangle.

proof.text: Construct each quotient augmentation degreewise as the extension/restriction-of-scalars unit followed by module sheafification. Restriction naturality follows from the pure-tensor formula for changeOfRingsMap, and the chain-map equation follows from naturality of the sheafification unit on id tensor d. Equality on all sections proves uniqueness.

Use the uniquely characterized quotient transition on the tensor 1 tensor m; the coefficient ring map preserves one. The unique augmentation formulas give strict compatibility. Project the product augmentation composed with 1 minus shift to each factor to obtain zero, so the zero homotopy gives the prescribed cocone lift. Mathlib mappingCocone.lift_fst and Pi.lift_π prove its quotient projections after localization.

Translate the epimorphism clause of countableProducts_exact into preservation of epimorphisms by the discrete-natural-number limit functor, hence CountableAB4Star. Apply derivedCategory_countableProducts_core in the standard derived localization to obtain the required product and its localized limiting cone. Transport across Discrete.compNatIsoDiscrete and identify the cone projections. The universal property of the chosen product makes the canonical comparison invertible.

Check the comparison intertwines the localized 1 minus shift with the derived tower transition endomorphism on every projection. Transport Mathlib mappingCocone_triangle_distinguished by the identity on the cocone and the product comparison on both product terms; the boundary is exactly the stipulated inverse comparison followed by the localized boundary.

For a strict map of towers use towerTransitionEndomorphism_natural_backward to form the commutative square of 1 minus shift. Shift Mathlib mappingCone.map by minus one. Its two coordinate equations follow from the cone inclusions and projections. The mappingCocone.id_X identity proves uniqueness from the two coordinates.
